hints: Identify the right-hand root to determine the least possible $n$.
walkthrough:
Set $f'(x) \ge 0$ for an increasing function and factorise the quadratic:
$$3(x^2 - 2x - 3) \ge 0 \implies 3(x - 3)(x + 1) \ge 0$$

Determine the right-hand interval where $f'(x) \ge 0$ and state the least value of $n$:
$$\text{The quadratic is positive for } x \ge 3 \text{ (and } x \le -1\text{)}$$
$$\text{For } x > n \text{ to be strictly increasing, the least possible value of } n \text{ is } n = 3$$

ai_rubric.Differentiation and Monotonicity: Differentiates to $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x - 9$ (B1). Sets $f'(x) \ge 0$ and factorises to $3(x-3)(x+1)$ (M1A1). Obtains least value $n = 3$ (A1).
